<<<d459ca81-643a-40b1-bcb3-dc2f4c860210>>>: dense green daytime jungle. 100% matches the reference.

Long dark curly hair gathered cleanly into a single bun/knot at the back of the head, pulled back off the face. No loose hair hanging over the face. Both ears are fully exposed, not covered by hair. An original tribal warrior styled after an Australian Aboriginal bush hunter: weathered desert look, natural earth presence. Hair long and tied back in a single bun, ears exposed with bone piercings. PHYSIQUE
Excellent athletic condition: lean, wiry, sinewy build with a dancer's flexibility, not bulky. Low body fat. Clearly defined abdominal muscles and a developed, well-built chest that read plainly. An original dystopian or fantasy desert warrior: weathered post-apocalyptic look, raw survival presence. SCENE CONTEXT
A character reference sheet for one original fictional post-apocalyptic survivor — a hardened wasteland drifter. Built on the face of the supplied reference person. Neutral studio reference layout showing the same single character across four defined shots for identity locking.
ANTI-CULTURE LOCK
The character is a fictional modern post-apocalyptic survivor with no ethnic or cultural identity. No indigenous, tribal, Native American, Maya, Aztec, Inca, Polynesian, Maori, or any real-world cultural references, motifs, dress, jewelry, body art, hairstyles, paint, or styling of any kind. No feathers, no bone jewelry, no loincloths, no ritual marks, no spirals/koru, no stepped frets or sun discs, no ceremonial items. Everything reads as improvised modern survival gear and contemporary abstract body art, never folk or tribal.
REALISM LOCK
Photorealistic live-action result, indistinguishable from a real photograph of a real human shot on a professional camera. A real flesh-and-blood man, not a 3D render, not CGI, not a game character, not animation, not cartoon, not stylized illustration, not painterly art. Real human anatomy, real skin, real hair, real fabric, natural photographic depth of field, real camera grain and color. Documentary-grade realism throughout.
REFERENCE FACE
The character's face is taken directly from the supplied reference photos: adult male, mid-20s to early-30s, warm medium-bronze skin, dark wavy hair in the reference color, full dark mustache with a small soul-patch tuft under the lower lip, dark brown eyes, broad straight nose, soft rounded jaw, faint moles on the cheeks. The face, complexion, and facial features must match the reference 100% in every shot. Expression carries quiet menace: a slightly sullen, defiant glare, brows lightly furrowed, jaw set, hard confident stare.
FACE LOCK
Keep the reference man's face unchanged: same bone structure, same mustache and chin tuft, same eyes, nose, and lips, same complexion and moles. Adjust only the expression to a hard, sullen, defiant look with lightly furrowed brows — do not change the underlying features or proportions. The face is completely clean: no face paint, no markings, no tattoos on the face or neck. Do not slim, age, or restyle the face. Keep the reference hair color, but the hair is longer than the reference and worn pulled back. Everything else about the face stays identical to the reference.
HAIR AND EARS
Long dark hair pulled back off the face and gathered into a simple low knot/tie at the back of the head. Hair texture is loosely wavy, not tightly curly and not straight — soft natural waves with gentle bends. From the tie, long wavy strands fall down the back of the head and neck. The hair looks unwashed and lived-in: slightly greasy and oily at the roots, sweat-dampened, with a dull low sheen, a few stray flyaways. The hairline and forehead are clean and exposed, no hair over the face. Both ears stay fully exposed and uncovered by hair. Ears are pierced with plain modern industrial jewelry only — matte black ceramic plugs or simple brushed-steel rings. No bone, tusk, horn, wood, or carved ornaments of any kind.
CHARACTER DESIGN
An original post-apocalyptic wasteland survivor: weathered, grimy, industrial-scavenger look, raw survival presence. Hair long and wavy, unwashed, tied back, face and ears exposed. Gear and accents look improvised from salvaged modern materials — canvas, webbing straps, metal buckles — never folk, ritual, or tribal. No headdress, no plumes, no traditional or ethnic items.
PHYSIQUE
Heavily muscled and powerfully built, in peak physical condition, dense lean working muscle on a medium-height frame. Strong, thick muscle mass with sharp, clearly defined relief across the whole body: large developed biceps and triceps, thick forearms, full square heavy pectorals, hard well-cut six-pack abdominals with pronounced obliques, broad thick shoulders and traps, muscular back, and strong powerful legs with defined quads and calves. Athletic, dense and imposing but still lean and flexible — a hardened fighter physique with low body fat and crisp muscle separation, clearly stronger than an average man, not soft bodybuilder bulk and not skinny.
TATTOOS
Extensive abstract tattoos in only two styles: heavy blackwork and dotwork — no other styles, no illustrative linework, no fractal/circuit graphics, no animals, no cultural or folk symbols, no runes, no spirals, no koru, no stepped frets or sun discs, no readable letters, and nothing that flows around the body in ritual-band fashion. Roughly 80% of the total body skin is covered in dense solid blackwork — large bold filled black panels and thick rectilinear/angular black masses across chest, stomach, full back, both arms, and both legs front and back (thighs, shins, and calves). The remaining ~20% is fine stippled dotwork: soft stippled gradients that feather and shade the edges of the black panels into the bare skin. The shapes are modern, asymmetric and graphic — sharp-edged abstract blocks and fields, not symmetrical tribal patterns. Both arms are fully sleeved from shoulder to wrist with no bare gaps. A single large centerpiece dominates the back: a massive solid blackwork mass with dotwork-shaded edges spanning between the shoulder blades down to the lower back. No tattoos on the face or neck. Reads as contemporary blackwork-and-dotwork body art, integrated into the skin, stretching over the muscle relief. Consistent placement and design across all shots.
TATTOO CONTINUITY LOCK
The chest, collarbone and upper-shoulder tattoos visible in the FRONT PORTRAIT (Shot 1) must be exactly the same design, placement, and pattern as the chest and shoulder tattoos in the FULL BODY FRONT (Shot 3). Same blackwork masses and same dotwork shading in both shots — the portrait and the full-body front view are the same body, so the overlapping tattooed areas match perfectly with no differences.
WARDROBE AND BODY
Bare torso, fully exposed muscular chest and stomach showing the tattoos and muscle relief. Legs mostly bare and exposed, showing the front and back leg tattoos. On the feet, simple wrapped canvas-and-strap foot coverings (improvised survival footwraps), not sandals and not bare-foot-only and never ritual or tribal.
Lower garment is an improvised utility wrap-kilt covering the groin and upper thighs — short, with shorts-level coverage. It is made of salvaged grey-brown canvas wound and folded around the hips, but clearly fastened and held by modern hardware: visible webbing straps, a metal buckle, and rough stitching. It reads as scavenged post-apocalyptic gear, NOT a folk loincloth, NOT a breechcloth, NOT fur, NOT tailored shorts. Worn and weathered: frayed edges, loose threads, dirt and dust stains, faded patchy color, pieced from mismatched fabric scraps. This wrap is the only lower garment. Modest coverage, nothing explicit.
SKIN AND DETAIL
Hyper-realistic skin texture: visible pores, fine surface grain, faint natural tone variation across the body, the reference cheek moles preserved. Skin looks matte and dry rather than oily — no glossy sweat sheen, no shiny highlights on the skin. A few old battle scars present — a pale healed slash across the ribs, a short scar on one forearm, a small mark on the brow — healed and natural, not bloody or fresh. Scars sit slightly raised or paler than surrounding skin. Skin reads as living tissue stretched over real working muscle, with natural creases at the joints.

REFERENCE FACE The character's face is taken directly from the supplied reference photos: adult male, mid-20s to early-30s, warm medium-bronze skin, dark wavy hair in the reference color, full dark mustache with a small soul-patch tuft under the lower lip, dark brown eyes, broad straight nose, soft rounded jaw, calm neutral gaze, faint moles on the cheeks. The face, complexion, and facial features must match the reference 100% in every shot.
FACE LOCK Keep the reference man's face unchanged: same bone structure, same mustache and chin tuft, same eyes, nose, and lips, same complexion and moles. War paint sits on top of this face without changing its features. Do not slim, age, or restyle the face. Keep the reference hair color, but the hair is longer than the reference and worn pulled back. Everything else about the face stays identical to the reference.
HAIR AND EARS Long dark hair pulled back off the face and gathered into a single high bun/top-knot at the back of the head. Hair texture is loosely wavy, not tightly curly and not straight — soft natural waves with gentle bends. From the bun, long wavy strands fall down the back of the head and neck. The hair looks unwashed and lived-in: slightly greasy and oily at the roots, sweat-dampened, with a dull low-sheen sheen rather than clean bounce, a few stray flyaways. The hairline and forehead are clean and exposed, no hair hanging over the face. Both ears stay fully exposed and uncovered by hair. Ears are pierced and stretched, with curved carved bone/tusk ornaments hanging through the lobes instead of metal earrings.
CHARACTER DESIGN An original tribal warrior styled after an Australian Aboriginal bush hunter: weathered desert look, natural earth presence. Hair long and wavy, unwashed and slightly greasy, pulled back into a single high bun with loose wavy strands falling behind, face and ears exposed, bone tusk ear ornaments. Simple primitive accents only — bone or wood ornaments. No feathered headdress, no ceremonial plumes, no modern items.
PHYSIQUE Excellent athletic condition: lean, wiry, sinewy build with a dancer's flexibility, not bulky. Low body fat. Clearly defined abdominal muscles and a developed, well-built chest that read plainly. Strong shoulders and forearms, visible muscle separation, taut skin over working muscle. Powerful but supple — a body built for climbing, running, and hunting, not a bodybuilder.
TATTOOS Extensive tribal tattoos covering chest, stomach, both arms and both legs, mixing heavy blackwork (bold solid black panels and thick bands), dotwork (fine stippled gradients and shaded geometric fields), and rune-style linework drawn from Turkic and Celtic runic motifs — angular Turkic runiform marks combined with interlaced Celtic knotwork and looping rune bands. Roughly 40% of the total body skin is covered in dense solid blackwork, the rest is rune linework and dotwork shading. Both arms are fully sleeved from shoulder to wrist with no bare gaps. A single large centerpiece tattoo dominates the back: a big turtle with a patterned shell filled with rune-knotwork and dotwork, spanning between the shoulder blades down to the lower back. Abstract decorative patterns and runic motifs only, no readable modern letters. Consistent placement and design across all shots.
WARDROBE AND BODY Bare torso, fully exposed chest and stomach showing the tattoos. Legs are mostly bare and exposed below the garment. Barefoot, no sandals, bare soles on the ground. Groin garment is a wrapped-cloth loincloth — NOT fur and NOT tailored shorts. A long strip of fabric wound and folded around the hips and between the legs, wrapping over the groin and the upper thighs so the covered area roughly matches the coverage of short shorts, while clearly reading as hand-wound draped fabric with visible folds, overlaps, and a knotted/tucked closure at the waist — not a sewn garment. The cloth is worn and weathered: frayed edges, loose threads, scattered dirt and dust stains, faded patchy color, and clearly pieced together from several mismatched scraps of fabric of slightly different earth tones and weaves stitched and tucked together. This wrap is the only garment. Modest coverage, nothing explicit. Face carries war paint: simple horizontal battle stripes across the cheeks and one stripe over the nose bridge, in charcoal-black and ochre-red, slightly smudged like applied by hand — painted over the reference face without hiding its features.
SKIN AND DETAIL Hyper-realistic skin texture: visible pores, fine surface grain, subtle sheen of sweat on the shoulders and chest, sun-weathered roughness, faint natural tone variation across the body, the reference cheek moles preserved. A few old battle scars present — a pale healed slash across the ribs, a short scar on one forearm, a small mark on the brow — healed and natural, not bloody or fresh. Scars sit slightly raised or paler than surrounding skin. Skin reads as living tissue over real muscle, with natural creases at the joints.
FORMAT MODE Single static character reference sheet, one consistent character, exactly four shots side by side, all the same person with identical reference face, hair bun, bone ear ornaments, tattoos, scars, paint, and cloth wrap.
FOUR SHOTS Shot 1 — FRONT PORTRAIT: head-and-shoulders close-up, facing camera, showing the reference face, wavy hair pulled back into the high bun with loose wavy strands falling behind, exposed pierced ears with bone tusk ornaments, mustache, war-paint stripes, brow scar, and the top of the chest tattoo. Shot 2 — PROFILE PORTRAIT: head-and-shoulders close-up in full side profile (90° turn), showing the nose-and-jaw profile line, the high bun and loose wavy strands falling at the back, the fully exposed ear with hanging bone tusk ornament, and the war-paint stripes from the side. Shot 3 — FULL BODY FRONT: full figure head to bare feet, facing camera straight on, arms relaxed at sides, weight even, full chest, stomach, fully sleeved arms and leg tattoos, abs and chest definition, and the cloth wrap covering groin and upper thighs visible. Shot 4 — FULL BODY BACK: full figure head to bare feet, back to camera, clearly showing the high bun with falling wavy strands, the large turtle centerpiece tattoo across the back, plus shoulder, arm and leg tattoos, and the rear of the wrapped cloth over the seat and upper thighs. Shots 3 and 4 at identical scale, feet aligned on the same ground line.
OPTICS Portrait shots (front and profile): 29° diagonal field of view, short telephoto portrait lens character, camera 4 to 6 meters, flattering stable face proportions, sharp subject, softly compressed background. Full-body shots: 47° diagonal field of view, standard normal lens character, camera 3 to 5 meters, natural human-eye perspective, zero distortion, true body proportions, full figure sharp head to bare feet.
CAMERA Eye-level, locked tripod, no movement, no perspective foreshortening. Even framing with equal headroom and floor space. Consistent subject height in both full-body shots and consistent head size in both portraits.
PHYSICS AND MATERIAL The wrapped cloth hangs with real fabric weight, visible weave, layered folds and overlaps over the hips and upper thighs, frayed scrap edges catching the light, the waist knot pressing slightly into the skin. The high bun holds its shape while loose wavy strands fall behind with natural weight; the unwashed, slightly oily hair clumps in soft heavier locks rather than light fluffy curls. Bone tusk ear ornaments hang with small weight. Tattoo ink sits flat on living skin and follows muscle curvature across chest, stomach, arms, back and legs. Bare feet make full flat contact with the floor, toes spread under body weight. War paint reads as matte hand-applied pigment, not digital overlay.
LIGHTING Clean neutral studio key from front-upper-left with soft fill, even exposure across all four shots, gentle shadow under the feet. Reference skin tone, face, muscle definition, scars, tattoo black, and paint colors stay accurate and consistent. No dramatic shadow, no color cast — a flat readable reference sheet.
POSITIVE LOCKS Same single invented character in all four shots, face 100% matching the reference photos (same mustache, eyes, nose, complexion, moles, hair color), identical tattoos, identical scars, identical cloth wrap, identical bone ear ornaments, identical war paint. Long dark loosely-wavy hair (not tightly curly, not straight), unwashed and slightly greasy and sweaty, pulled back into a single high bun with loose wavy strands falling behind, forehead and face clean, both ears fully exposed and pierced with curved carved bone tusk ornaments. Lean wiry-muscular athletic build with readable abs and developed chest, flexible and supple. Original tribal warrior styled after an Australian Aboriginal bush hunter. Tattoos cover chest, stomach, arms, legs and back, mixing blackwork, dotwork and Turkic/Celtic rune motifs; both arms fully sleeved; roughly 40% of the body in solid blackwork; large turtle centerpiece tattoo on the back. Groin garment is hand-wound draped cloth pieced from worn, dirty, frayed fabric scraps, covering groin and upper thighs with shorts-level coverage but never sewn shorts and never fur.

A colossal ancient banyan-like tree stands at the center of a deep tropical rainforest, seen from a high aerial vantage angled 45 degrees downward so that both its broad fanning crown and the vast web of gnarled surface roots radiating across the forest floor read at once. The massive fluted, buttressed trunk widens at the base; thick heavy low branches spread outward horizontally into a wide symmetrical crown, with long curtains of aerial prop roots hanging down like columns, some reaching the ground to form secondary trunks. Bark and roots are cloaked in moss and lichen and draped with hanging vines and epiphytes. A faint, slightly-trodden dirt footpath winds through the dense foreground undergrowth of ferns, monstera and banana leaves toward the trunk, while weathered, moss-covered stone blocks lie scattered chaotically through the misty background depth between other tall rainforest trees that are slightly smaller but still high — dense foliage packing the frame with no empty space.
It is early morning in a remote, untouched equatorial rainforest, humid after rain in the wet season, with traces of a forgotten ruin. Soft overcast canopy diffusion lets god-rays break through the mist over the crown from above, with cool ambient fill and subtle warm highlights where sunlight catches moss on the branches and roots. The palette is cool-leaning and desaturated with a green-teal grade — deep forest green, moss emerald, teal shadow, wet bark umber, misty grey-white and muted gold shafts. The mood is ancient, humid, hushed, immense, primeval and foreboding.
Shot as a photorealistic cinematic movie still in the style of tropical realism and lost-world expedition cinema, echoing Hoyte van Hoytema. Extreme wide framing on an ARRI ALEXA Mini LF with a Cooke S7i 24mm lens, 2.39:1 Cinemascope, slow descending push-in over the crown and down onto the roots. Deep focus keeps everything sharp from the crown and foreground footpath to the distant stone blocks, softened only by natural mist. Wet moss and lichen on fluted bark and gnarled roots, fibrous stringy aerial roots in curtains, glossy rain-beaded leaves, damp dark soil on the worn path, weathered granular stone. Floating mist, atmospheric perspective, suspended moisture and faint drifting spores in the light beams, with fine low film grain, soft bloom on the light shafts, slight halation, subtle chromatic aberration at the edges and gentle vignetting.

Massive weathered stone blocks lie half-swallowed by dense jungle, their flat tops forming a broken stepping path that leads through thick undergrowth into the depth of the frame. The colossal quarried megaliths are cracked and tilted at irregular angles, their carved edges softened by centuries, coated in thick velvet moss and creeping vines, with ferns and roots wedged into the seams between them. The jungle presses in as walls on both sides, and beyond the path more overgrown stone emerges from a green misty background, dense foliage filling the frame with no empty space.
It is midday in a remote equatorial rainforest, humid and still in the wet season — a forgotten ancient site reclaimed by nature. Soft dappled canopy light filters down with cool shadow fill and the occasional warm patch striking moss on the stone, no hard key. The palette is cool-leaning and desaturated with a green-teal grade — moss green, wet stone grey, teal shade, umber crevices, pale mist and muted olive. The mood is mysterious, ancient, overgrown, silent, weighty and expectant.

Granular weathered granite, thick velvet moss, glossy wet leaves, damp earth in the seams and fibrous vine tendrils, all under hanging humidity haze with atmospheric perspective and a damp sheen on the stone. Fine low film grain, subtle chromatic aberration, gentle vignetting and faint halation in the mist.

A cinematic 35mm film photograph of a narrow dirt jungle trail winding through dense tropical vegetation and ending abruptly at the edge of a high rocky cliff. Ferns, hanging lianas and broad wet leaves frame both sides of the path, opening up at the precipice where the rock drops away into a vast misty jungle valley far below, endless rainforest canopy fading into atmospheric haze toward the horizon. Late-afternoon sunlight rakes across the cliff edge, backlighting drifting mist rising from the valley, a few loose stones at the rim of the drop. Shot from low on the trail looking toward the cliff edge, strong sense of depth and vertigo, no people. Lush greens against pale hazy blue distance, soft film grain, tense adventure-film mood.

Same super-wide top-down 45-degree style, holding the green-teal grade — here's location 3 in plain text:
A narrow jungle trail winds forward through thick foliage toward an abrupt cliff edge, seen from a high aerial vantage angled 45 degrees downward so that both the winding path and the sheer drop into a vast misty valley beyond read at once.
